I am 66 years old this year, and I have been farming these lands since I was 21. My father taught me, and now my wife and I manage 15 mu together. Our two children have left for the city, so it is just the two of us. I never went to school, but I know this land well—better than any book.

This year, I will keep my usual arrangement because it has fed us for decades. I will put **10 mu into the wheat-maize rotation** and **5 mu into cotton**. Why? The wheat and maize give us steady grain and straw, and I can machine-harvest both. Cotton pays better per mu, but it is heavy work—my old back can still handle 5 mu of pruning and spraying, but no more. With only two mouths to feed and well water I can pump myself, this is the balance I trust.

For **winter wheat** on the 10 mu: I will buy improved seed from the township shop—maybe a variety like Jimai or Luyuan, the kind that yields around 1000 jin per mu if the weather is fair. In early October, after the maize comes off, I will hire the rotary tiller to prepare the seedbed. I will spread basal compound fertilizer (about 18 jin of nitrogen worth, plus phosphorus and potassium) and drill the seed. Wheat needs water at three critical times: the overwinter irrigation around freezing, then again at jointing in March, and once more at heading in April. I will spray four times total—herbicide once after sowing, then insecticide and fungicide when the aphids and rust appear in spring. I expect about 1000 kg per mu.

For **summer maize** on the same 10 mu: As soon as the wheat is threshed in early June, I will plant hybrid maize seed—Denghai or something similar—directly without tilling. There is no time to waste between wheat harvest and maize sowing; if you plough, you might miss the rain window. Maize is greedy for nitrogen, so I will put down compound fertilizer at planting and side-dress urea when the plants are knee-high. Two irrigations are usually enough with summer rain: one at the seven-leaf stage and one at tasseling. Three pesticide rounds—herbicide, then insecticide for corn borers. Hybrid maize should give me about 1100 kg per mu.

For **cotton** on the 5 mu: I will rotary-till in late April and sow improved cotton seed—maybe Guoxinmian or 99-1, the kind with the bug-resistant trait, though I still have to watch for worms. Cotton needs more potassium than grain, so I favor a compound with higher K. I will irrigate three times: at seedling, flowering, and boll-setting. I will spray pesticides about eight times—cotton attracts more insects than grain, but I am old enough to know when spraying is truly needed rather than doing it every week like some young farmers. I aim for 500 kg of seed cotton per mu. Any more would be a gift from heaven.

I do not chase the highest yield in the village. I chase the yield my wife and I can actually bring home without breaking ourselves or the well.
